sections.text: In this fictional arithmetic example, a basket earns 100 units before expenses. A cost of 4 units leaves 96 units. A cost of 1 unit leaves 99 units. The two baskets have identical gross proceeds.

The identical-proceeds assumption can fail. In a separate fictional example, basket A earns 110 units and costs 4 units, leaving 106. Basket B earns 100 units and costs 1 unit, leaving 99. Cost alone does not determine the winner.
